claims.text: Each EF degree of damage has an expected, lower-bound and upper-bound wind speed set by expert elicitation (means of the experts' estimates); the expected value assumes normal conditions (no weak links, traditional construction, code compliance, maintenance) and the bounds cover deviations from them.
claims.update_trigger: A revised EF scale (e.g. ASCE/SEI 49-21 implementation) changes the tables.

claims.text: EF wind speeds are three-second gusts estimated at the point of damage; the estimates vary with height and exposure.
claims.update_trigger: A source states the reference height and exposure.

claims.text: FR12 (one- and two-family residences, 1,000-5,000 ft2) has ten degrees of damage, expected gust 65 to 200 mph (table in EF_DEGREE_OF_DAMAGE_TABLE).
claims.update_trigger: Table revision.

claims.text: MBS (metal building systems; examples warehouses; large overhead doors; rigid frames, purlins, x-bracing) has eight degrees of damage, expected gust 67 to 155 mph.
claims.update_trigger: Table revision; profile changes to tilt-up.

claims.text: LRB (low-rise building, 1-4 stories; examples office buildings; steel or concrete frame; BUR, single-ply or metal roof) has seven degrees of damage, expected gust 68 to 188 mph.
claims.update_trigger: Table revision.

claims.text: FEMA assumes the damage states None, Slight, Moderate, Extensive and Complete correspond to mean building loss ratios of 0, 2, 10, 50 and 100%, identified from the damage descriptions with expert judgment, and interpolates linearly over 0-2, 2-5, 5-10, 10-50 and 50-100%.
claims.update_trigger: A source gives repair cost per EF degree of damage.

claims.text: Hazus residential damage states: Slight = at most one window/door/garage door, roof cover loss over 2% to 15%; Moderate = roof cover over 15% to 50%, 1 to 3 deck panels; Extensive = roof cover over 50%, deck over 3 panels to 25%; Destruction = roof structure or wall frame failure.

Hazus metal-building damage states: Slight = one door or window; Moderate = slight roof or wall panel failures; Extensive = extensive window damage or roof sheathing loss, some frame damage likely; Destruction = significant roof and wall panel failures, significant frame damage.

Hazus engineered steel building damage states: Slight = one window or door, roof cover over 2% to 15%; Moderate = roof cover over 15% to 50%, windows over one to 2%, one or two deck panels; Extensive = roof cover over 50%, deck over two panels to 25%, local joist failures; Destruction = essentially complete roof failure or more than 25% of sheathing, wall envelope opened.

An EF degree of damage is a damage description, not a repair-cost ratio; the cost assigned to each degree in this cell is a judgment through the Hazus damage states (below-Slight = 1%, single-vs-multiple glazing = 5%, house shifted off its foundation = Extensive).
claims.update_trigger: A repair-cost study by EF degree; claims data by EF rating.

claims.text: Reading LB-UB as a 90% range (beta = ln(UB/LB)/3.29) gives beta 0.09 to 0.13; reading it as 68% or 95% changes the house damage at 120 mph from 36% to 41% or 34% (tornado).
claims.update_trigger: A source states the bound percentile.

claims.text: Hazard delivers, for straight-line wind, an ASCE 7-22 3-second gust at 10 m, Exposure C (events at or above 58 mph, exponential excess, capped at 113 m/s = 252.8 mph) and, for a tornado, the EF band midpoint gust (75, 98, 123, 150.5, 183, 227 mph), with national median path length and width and a 150 km pooling radius.
claims.update_trigger: Hazard changes its fields or bounds.

claims.text: On Hazard's grid, the median cell sees 0.66 straight-line gust events a year at or above 58 mph, and the ASCE 700-year gust rebuilt from the layer is 99 / 107 / 113 mph (10th percentile / median / 90th percentile; maximum 167).
claims.update_trigger: Hazard changes its severity model.

claims.text: Without an onset, straight-line yearly building loss is 370 to 500 times NRI (median cell); with the 96 mph onset it is 13 to 35 times; an onset at 90% of each cell's design gust gives about the same (13 to 36 times). Rank correlation with NRI is about 0.5.
claims.update_trigger: Hazard revises the straight-line frequency; a building-level loss record.

claims.text: Tornado yearly building loss on Hazard's grid is 0.11 to 0.26 times NRI with rank correlation 0.91; the gap comes from Hazard's frequency and median path geometry, not the curve (a direct hit at the EF2 midpoint gust, 123 mph, already gives 18-44% damage and at EF3, 150.5 mph, 46-96%).
claims.update_trigger: Hazard revises tornado path dimensions.

claims.text: The existing straight-line convective solar curve gives zero damage below R0 = 0.70 to 0.90 of the design pressure ratio, i.e. below 84% to 95% of the design gust.
The repository's failure-mode list names tornado or straight-line wind represented by a boolean or curve shift, and an unsupported pathway borrowing a neighbouring curve, as defects.
The EF scale was built from tornado damage; the report does not address straight-line wind, and no source found establishes the EF degree-of-damage speeds for straight-line convective wind.
claims.locator: whole report (no straight-line or downburst mention)
claims.update_trigger: A straight-line damage survey or loss study by building type.

claims.text: A documented repository precedent reuses a hurricane response for straight-line wind and tornado as a T4 cross-hazard proxy without duration conversion and with the EF midpoint gust as a T4 bridge.

claims.text: All Hazus hurricane damage and loss functions are indexed to the peak gust at 10 m in open terrain (z0 = 0.03 m), not to one-minute sustained wind; terrain enters as a separate curve family.
claims.locator: S001 §4.3 p. 4-81 and §5.5.1.3 p. 5-173; S003 Demand-Type "Peak Gust Wind Speed", mph
claims.update_trigger: A Hazus edition re-indexes its functions.

claims.text: The Hazus building damage and loss functions predict the combined effects of wind pressure, windborne debris and rainwater penetration; most interior damage comes from rain entering through roof, fenestration or cladding damage.
claims.update_trigger: A source separates the mechanisms.

claims.text: Tree-blowdown damage is an additive term applied to building and contents losses of small residential buildings only; it is not inside the base building loss functions.
claims.locator: S001 §2.1 p. 2-4 and §8.2; S002 sheets huTreeBlowdownFunctions and huTreeBlowdownLossFunctions
claims.update_trigger: Hazard supplies tree height, type and density; JL adds the house add-on.

claims.text: The building loss ratio is repair cost over the total replacement cost of the building (subassembly cost ratios sum over the whole building); commercial losses include a 1.25 repair-and-replacement factor and a 1.20 overhead-and-profit factor and are capped at total replacement cost. The default residence value includes site preparation for the slab.
claims.update_trigger: A per-area value source with a different boundary is selected.

claims.text: Hazus publishes each variant for five terrain classes (z0 0.03, 0.15, 0.35, 0.70, 1.00 m) and assigns a census-tract roughness from NLCD weighted by building area; the manual states no rule for combining the five classes for intermediate roughness.
claims.locator: S001 §4.3.4 pp. 4-64 to 4-65 (Equation 4-19); S002 sheet huTerrain; no interpolation rule found in a full-text search of S001
claims.update_trigger: Hazard adds a roughness field and a mapping rule is agreed, or FEMA documents interpolation.

claims.text: WSF1 is the wood single-family one-story building type; for the continental US (CaseID 1) it has 160 variants: roof shape (hip, gable), secondary water resistance (yes, no), roof-deck attachment (6d @ 6"/12", 8d @ 6"/12", 6d/8d mix @ 6"/6", 8d @ 6"/6"), roof-to-wall connection (toe-nail, strap), garage door (none, weak, standard; none or SFBC 1994 with shutters), shutters (yes, no); roof cover shingle.
claims.locator: S001 Table C-1 p. C-1; S002 huListOfWindBldgTypes rows with sbtName WSF1, CaseID 1; huListOfBldgChar
claims.parameter_or_rule: house building type and characteristic options

claims.text: SECBL (steel engineered commercial, 1-2 stories) and MECBL (masonry engineered commercial, 1-2 stories) have identical building loss functions for every characteristic combination and terrain; their characteristics are roof cover (BUR, SPM), window area (low, medium, high), shutters, windborne-debris environment (A residential/commercial, B varies by direction, C residential, D none) and metal-deck attachment (standard, superior).
claims.locator: S001 Table C-1 p. C-1 to C-2 and §5.6.6 p. 5-241; S002 rows SECBL and MECBL (480 curves each, identical); S003 S.ECB.L and M.ECB.L

claims.text: SPMBL is the large pre-engineered steel metal building (more than 50,000 ft2); SPMBM covers 4,000-50,000 ft2 and SPMBS 4,000 ft2 or less. Characteristics: roof-deck age (new or average, old), shutters, metal-deck attachment (standard, superior).
claims.locator: S001 §9.1 p. 9-2 and Table C-1 p. C-2; S002 rows SPMBL
claims.update_trigger: JL fixes a reference floor area below 50,000 ft2 (then SPMBM).

claims.text: MLRM1 is a masonry low-rise strip mall up to 15 ft high; MLRI is a masonry low-rise warehouse/factory 20 ft high. Both are recorded alternatives, not selected.
claims.update_trigger: Owner adds a masonry strip-mall or masonry warehouse profile.

claims.text: Most common characteristic values (Hazus 7.0 Table C-2, average over all 49 regions): WSF1 gable 78.6%, no SWR 99.8%, 6d @ 6"/12" 41.5% (8d @ 6"/6" 32.1%, 8d @ 6"/12" 26.4%), toe-nail 78.6%, no garage 52.1%, no shutters 95.8%; SECBL BUR 89.4%, low window area 67.7%, debris environment B 41.1%, standard metal deck 99.6%, no shutters 95.7%; SPMBL old roof deck 88.1%, standard metal deck 99.5%, no shutters 97.4%.
claims.locator: Table C-2 pp. C-3 to C-4 (WSF1), p. C-20 (SPMBL), pp. C-21 to C-22 (SECBL)
claims.update_trigger: A regional reference building is defined, or JL chooses a typical mix.

claims.text: The building-loss ordinates of the FEMA Hazus 6.1 extract equal SimCenter's separately extracted Hazus 5.1 copy exactly, for all 1,840 compared curves (WSF1 CONUS 800, SECBL 480, MECBL 480, SPMBL 40, SPMBM 40) at all 41 speeds.
claims.update_trigger: A discrepancy appears in a later extract.

claims.text: The Hazus 6.1 and 7.0 hurricane updates concern the building-type and characteristic mapping schemes (49 regions, NSI-based weights); the manual does not describe changes to the damage or loss functions.
claims.update_trigger: FEMA publishes a 7.x function extract or release notes change the functions.

claims.text: The extract's default-mapping sheets (huBldgMapping, huGBSMapping) use the 12 pre-6.1 regions (Florida_Central … Southeast_Inland), not the 49 regions of Hazus 6.1 and 7.0.
claims.locator: S002 huBldgMapping.huBldgSchemeName (12 values); S001 §9.7 p. 9-49 (49 regions from 6.1)

claims.text: The 15 selected records are 0 at 50 mph, never exceed 1.0, and are non-decreasing except for twelve dips of at most 0.0020 (0.2 points), all at 205-235 mph (house suburban and light-trees; commercial open, light-suburban and suburban).
claims.locator: CURVE_ORDINATES; validator check "selected records: dips <= 0.002 and only above 200 mph"
claims.update_trigger: A dip above 0.005 appears in a selected record.

claims.text: Across the whole extract, about half of the building-loss rows dip somewhere as wind rises (largest dip 0.10; 1% of rows dip more than 0.027) and 525 WSF1 values exceed 1.0 by at most 0.000052.

The SPMB superior metal-deck (rd110) rows are inconsistent: each old-deck superior curve exactly equals a new-deck superior curve of another size class, and SPMBL old-deck superior loses more than standard (0.815 vs 0.395 at 120 mph, open). The selected SPMBL old-deck standard row (wbID 1729) duplicates no other row.
claims.locator: S002 wbIDs 4813-4818 and 4951-4956 versus 1725-1730; same values in S003 S.PMB.*
claims.update_trigger: FEMA corrects or explains the rows.

claims.text: The selected SPMBL row moves in the directions the manual reports for metal buildings: large above medium, old deck above new (Table 5-77: medium to large +57% average damage state; 50% deck capacity reduction +23%). SPMBS standard rows are higher than SPMBM and SPMBL at 120 mph, against the manual's small-to-medium direction.
claims.locator: S001 Tables 5-76 and 5-77 p. 5-241; VARIANT_SENSITIVITY rows RE_IND_WAREHOUSE
claims.parameter_or_rule: plausibility check of the warehouse record
claims.update_trigger: FEMA corrects the SPMB family.

claims.text: Terrain is material: at 120 mph the reference house loses 31.3% in open terrain and 9.3% in suburban terrain; the warehouse 39.5% and 12.7%; the commercial building 8.8% and 5.7%.

Single-characteristic changes move the reference house at 140 mph (open) from 77.9% to: shutters 47.7%, straps 72.4%, 8d @ 6"/6" 69.4%, SWR 73.9%, all four 6.8%; commercial shutters 31.3% to 12.7%; warehouse shutters 88.2% to 35.1%.
claims.update_trigger: A resiliency measure is scoped for real estate.

claims.text: Hazard delivers a 3-second peak gust at 10 m in mph, open terrain, from STORM 10-minute wind × (1/0.88) × 1.20; thresholds 20-75 m/s give about 61-229 mph; the generic damage loader routes by unique selector match and checks one pathway-level valid_range on preferred_input_field.
claims.update_trigger: Hazard changes its delivered field or loader.

claims.text: The extract also publishes contents loss (DamLossDescID 6), loss of use in days (7) and damage-state probabilities (1-4) per variant and terrain.
claims.update_trigger: Contents enter scope.

claims.text: Hazus commercial roof cover options are BUR and SPM, both low-slope membranes; the SPMB metal-building type has no roof-cover characteristic (its roof is the metal-building roof system).
claims.locator: S002 huListOfBldgChar rows 4-5; SPMB charDescription tokens

claims.text: The legacy residential hurricane array has no gust averaging period, height, terrain or building type and saturates near 37% at 120 m/s; the second legacy array is straight-line wind.

For the selected commercial variant, light-suburban terrain gives higher building loss than open terrain at 90-250 mph (e.g. 27.7% vs 18.6% at 130 mph), and the open-terrain curve levels off at 88.3%; the house and warehouse records fall with rougher terrain at every speed.

claims.text: SECBM is the steel engineered commercial building of 3-5 stories (SECBL 1-2, SECBH 6 or more); the extract publishes 96 SECBM variants. For single-ply membrane, medium window area, no shutters, debris environment B and standard metal deck, SECBM and MECBM (masonry) give the same loss ratio at 100-160 mph in open and suburban terrain.
claims.locator: TM Appendix B building-type list (PDF p. 678, 33_SECBM); extract huListOfWindBldgTypes wbID 1840; VARIANT_SENSITIVITY_tropical_cyclone_wind_real_estate__model_v0_2__docs_r1.csv

claims.text: Hazus SPMB (pre-engineered metal building) characteristics are roof-deck age, shutters and metal-deck attachment only; there is no characteristic for large overhead doors, so the profile's eight 12 x 14 ft unprotected doors cannot change the curve.
claims.locator: Hazus 7.0 TM WBC list p. 9-32; extract huListOfWindBldgTypes SPMBL (8 variants)

claims.text: Hazus assigns house roof-deck attachment and roof-to-wall connection from the building code, design wind speed, design terrain and code year, so a 20-year-old house is code-built (8d nails, straps) only where its local code required it. On the source curves, 8d @ 6"/12" with straps reads 19.0% at 120 mph open (reference 31.3%) and 21.5% at 140 mph suburban (reference 51.2%).

claims.text: The USFS Wildfire Risk to Communities conditional risk to potential structures applies, per FSim flame-length class FLP1 to FLP6, a structure loss of 25/40/55/70/85/100 (tree), 20/35/50/65/80/95 (shrub) and 10/25/40/55/70/85 (grass/herbaceous), where 0 is no damage and 100 is complete loss.
claims.update_trigger: A revised WRC edition changes the response.

claims.text: The response represents 'the relative effect of wildfire on structures (i.e., relative degree of damage or loss)' and cRPS is 'essentially conditional Net Value Change' for a house; WRC uses it as a 0-100 index to rank places.

The three response functions 'reflect the assumption that consequence is greatest in tree fuels, lower in shrubs, and lowest in grass fuels'; the record gives no derivation, elicitation or field calibration for the numbers.
claims.update_trigger: A published derivation or field test of the response.

claims.text: Reading the WRC loss value as repair cost / structure replacement cost new of the same building.
claims.update_trigger: A cost-based statement from the source.

claims.text: FSim flame-length classes are FLP1 < 2 ft, FLP2 2-<4, FLP3 4-<6, FLP4 6-<8, FLP5 8-<12, FLP6 12+ ft, conditional on a fire; WRC's FLEP4 and FLEP8 are sums of its FLP classes above 4 and 8 ft, so WRC uses the same class boundaries (at 30 m, WildEST) as Hazard's 270 m FSim product.
claims.update_trigger: Hazard switches flame-length product.

claims.text: Hazard delivers, per 0.25-degree cell, an annual burn probability on burnable pixels (lambda = -ln(1-BP)) and the conditional FLP1-6 mix; it looks up damage at the exact class state (0 = no event), rejects fractional states and a burn probability in the damage call, and couples with p_hit = 1.
claims.update_trigger: Hazard changes its fields.

claims.text: Hazard does not deliver the fuel lifeform (tree, shrub, grass) that the WRC response depends on.
claims.update_trigger: Hazard adds a lifeform per cell (e.g. from LANDFIRE EVT).

claims.text: Among 12,188 inspected one-storey wood/vinyl/combustible-sided asphalt-roof houses in DINS (2013-2025), 58.7% were destroyed and 36.5% undamaged; of those damaged, 92.4% were destroyed. Mean damage (band midpoints, destroyed = 100%) is 0.59 over all fires, 0.29 in fires recording at least 20% no-damage, 0.33 without the Camp Fire, 0.65 without the 2025 Los Angeles fires.
claims.parameter_or_rule: house level check; near all-or-nothing outcome
claims.update_trigger: A DINS record with local fire intensity.

claims.text: Within the same fires, metal-wall metal-roof commercial buildings lost 0.79 times as much as those houses (258 buildings, 38 fires; 90% range 0.61-0.99) and multi-storey stucco/brick/cement commercial buildings 0.93 times (204 buildings, 17 fires; 0.66-1.38). Pooled over all fires the ratios are 0.30 and 0.42, and 0.27-0.60 and 0.28-0.81 across subsets.
claims.update_trigger: A loss study of large sprinklered warehouses or offices in wildfires.

claims.text: DINS commercial groups are California commercial buildings of any size and use; the reference warehouse (100,000 ft2, sprinklered) and office (54,000 ft2, sprinklered) are larger and DINS records no sprinkler or size field.
claims.update_trigger: Size- or sprinkler-stratified loss data.

claims.text: In DINS 2013-2018, building features that block ember entry (enclosed eaves, vent screens, multi-pane windows) explained more of survival than defensible space; any single variable explained little; many 'fire-safe' structures were destroyed.
claims.parameter_or_rule: why flame length is a weak predictor

claims.text: The house profile has a vented attic with no ember-resistant vent rating, vinyl siding and asphalt shingles; it declares no vegetation buffer or neighbouring buildings. These match the DINS house group and carry no mitigation credit.

On Hazard's grid the curves give yearly building loss 2.0x (house), 1.6x (warehouse) and 1.8x (office) NRI nationally (median cell 3.0x, 2.4x, 2.7x), rank correlation 0.88; the West is at 1.75x and the East at 4.7x (median cell, house).
